source: original (warmup: evaluate logs with integer/rational answers; apply log laws to expressions in log_a b)

parts.label: a_ii
parts.tolerance: Accept 2/3 or 0.667 (3 s.f.).

parts.label: a_iii
parts.tolerance: Accept -3 only (sign required).

parts.label: a_iv
parts.tolerance: Accept 3/4 or 0.75.

parts.label: b_i
parts.description: Write log_a(a^3 b) in terms of L = log_a b.
parts.tolerance: Accept 3 + L or log_a b + 3.
parts.notes: A1 for 3 + log_a b. Uses product rule: log_a(a^3) + log_a(b).

parts.label: b_ii
parts.description: Write log_a(b^2 / a) in terms of L = log_a b.
parts.tolerance: Accept 2L - 1 or -1 + 2 log_a b.
parts.notes: A1 for 2 log_a b - 1. Uses quotient + power rules.

parts.label: b_iii
parts.description: Write log_a sqrt(a^3 b) in terms of L = log_a b.
parts.tolerance: Accept 3/2 + (1/2) L, or (1/2)(3 + log_a b), or (3 + log_a b)/2.
parts.notes: A1 for 3/2 + (1/2) log_a b. Uses sqrt as ^(1/2), then product + power rules.

parts.label: b_iv
parts.description: Write log_(a^3) b in terms of L = log_a b.
parts.tolerance: Accept L/3 or (log_a b)/3.
parts.notes: A1 for (1/3) log_a b. Uses change-of-base: log_(a^3) b = log_a b / log_a a^3 = L/3.

source: original (simplify expressions using inverse identities ln(e^x) = x and e^(ln x) = x)

parts.label: a
parts.notes: A1 for 4. Inverse identity ln(e^x) = x.

parts.label: b
parts.notes: A1 for 7. Inverse identity e^(ln x) = x.

parts.label: c
parts.tolerance: Accept 2x+1 or 1+2x.
parts.notes: A1 for 2x + 1. Inverse identity applied to expression-valued exponent.

parts.label: d
parts.tolerance: Accept 8 only.
parts.notes: M1 for rewriting 3 ln 2 = ln 2^3 = ln 8 (or for (e^(ln 2))^3 = 2^3). A1 for 8.

source: original (solve simple e^x and ln equations; exact answers in terms of e or ln)

parts.label: a
parts.tolerance: Accept ln 12 or log_e 12. Numerical 2.4849... not required for full credit; exact form expected.
parts.notes: A1 for x = ln 12. Direct application of taking ln of both sides.

parts.label: b
parts.tolerance: Accept e^5. Numerical 148.4... not required for full credit.
parts.notes: A1 for x = e^5. Direct application of exponentiating both sides.

parts.label: c
parts.tolerance: Accept (1 + ln 9)/2, 1/2 + ln 3, or (1 + 2 ln 3)/2 (all equivalent).
parts.notes: M1 for taking ln to get 2x - 1 = ln 9. A1 for x = (1 + ln 9)/2 or equivalent simplified form.

parts.label: d
parts.tolerance: Accept (e^2 - 1)/3.
parts.notes: M1 for exponentiating to get 3x + 1 = e^2. A1 for x = (e^2 - 1)/3.

source: original (exponential growth: bacteria N(t) = 250 e^(kt), N(3) = 1000)

parts.label: b
parts.tolerance: Show that k = (1/3) ln 4 (answer given). Accept also k = ln(4^(1/3)) or k = (ln 4)/3.
parts.notes: M1 for substituting t=3, N=1000 to get 1000 = 250 e^(3k). A1 for simplifying to e^(3k) = 4. A1 (AG) for taking ln to obtain 3k = ln 4 and dividing by 3.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find N(5) to the nearest integer.
parts.tolerance: Accept 2519 or 2520 depending on rounding. Exact form 250 * 4^(5/3) acceptable as intermediate.
parts.notes: M1 for substituting t=5 into 250 e^(kt) (using k = (1/3) ln 4 or equivalent). A1 for evaluating e^(5k) = 4^(5/3) ≈ 10.079. A1 for N(5) ≈ 2520.

parts.label: d
parts.tolerance: Accept exact form t = 3 ln(40) / ln(4) or ln(40)/k. Numerical: 7.98 (3 s.f.). Accept also 7.99 with rounding mention. Graphing-calculator intersect/solver methods earn full credit.
parts.notes: M1 for setting 250 e^(kt) = 10000 and isolating to e^(kt) = 40. M1 for taking ln to get t = ln(40)/k = 3 ln(40)/ln(4). A1 for t ≈ 7.98 hours (3 s.f.). M1+M1 may also be awarded for a GDC-based solve.

parts.label: e
parts.description: Find the doubling time of the population (3 s.f.).
parts.tolerance: Accept exact form t = 3/2 = 1.5 hours, or equivalently 3 ln 2 / ln 4. Numerical: 1.50 (3 s.f.).
parts.notes: M1 for setting up doubling condition 2 = e^(kt). M1 for isolating t = ln(2)/k = 3 ln 2 / ln 4 = 3/2. A1 for t = 1.50 hours.

source: original (continuous compound interest A(t) = 5000 e^(0.06 t); compare with annual compounding for part d)

parts.label: a
parts.tolerance: Accept $6356.25 or 6356.25 (with or without $ sign). 5000 * e^0.24.
parts.notes: M1 for substituting t=4 into 5000 e^(0.06 t). A1 for $6356.25 (rounding 6356.2457... to nearest cent).

parts.label: b
parts.tolerance: Accept exact form t = ln(1.6)/0.06 or (50/3) ln(1.6). Numerical: 7.83 (3 s.f.). Graphing-calculator solve methods earn full credit.
parts.notes: M1 for setting 5000 e^(0.06 t) = 8000 and isolating to e^(0.06 t) = 1.6. M1 for taking ln to get t = ln(1.6)/0.06. A1 for t ≈ 7.83 years (3 s.f.).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find doubling time for the continuous account (3 s.f.).
parts.tolerance: Accept exact form t = ln(2)/0.06 or (50/3) ln 2. Numerical: 11.6 (3 s.f.). Accept 11.55 with rounding mention.
parts.notes: M1 for setting up 2 = e^(0.06 t). M1 for taking ln to isolate t = ln(2)/0.06. A1 for t ≈ 11.6 years (3 s.f.).

parts.label: d
parts.description: Find value of second account (annual compounding 6%) after 4 years, and difference from continuous account. Both to nearest cent.
parts.tolerance: Accept annual value $6312.38. Accept difference $43.86 or $43.87 (depending on whether subtraction uses rounded or unrounded values; 6356.25 - 6312.38 = 43.87, while unrounded gives 43.86).
parts.notes: M1 for setting up 5000 (1.06)^4. A1 for $6312.38. M1 for subtracting the two account values. A1 for difference $43.86 or $43.87 (both accepted).
parts.follow_through: Award the second M1 and A1 for difference even if candidate's value in (a) was incorrect — accept any difference computed correctly from candidate's continuous-account value and their annual value.
